title: How to become a referee
summary: You become a referee through a course and an exam at your national federation. International events ask for more: experience and, for the chief referee, a FITASC qualification.

body.html: The referee is central to any competition. The referee looks after safety and order on the stand and decides, on their own, whether a target was hit. Without referees there is no event, so clubs and federations welcome new people.

The first step is your country's national federation. It usually runs referee courses: rules theory, practice on the stand and an exam. After the exam you get a referee certificate or card. The procedure, length and requirements differ by country, so ask your federation or club first.

html.sporting: Each referee holds a valid certificate from their national federation. Without it, a person may only be an assistant referee, and only if the jury agrees in advance. The jury is the small group of officials who oversee the competition and settle disputes. The chief referee of an international event needs an international certificate issued by FITASC.
html.compak: The jury approves each referee before the start, and each holds a valid card from their national federation. Referees with little international experience work under the eye of international referees. The chief referee (the Compak® Sporting rules call this person the Head Referee) needs an international card and the FITASC qualification for that role.

body.html: International refereeing is the next level. Your federation will explain what it requires.

At international events referees make a formal promise. They promise to apply the rules, to judge honestly and impartially, and to set aside their own nationality and federation. That sums up the job: calm, knowledge of the rules and respect for each shooter.

A tip to start: ask to help an experienced referee at club shoots. You will see the work from the inside, and the rules will stick much faster. The decisions themselves, in plain words: What counts as a hit, and what a No Bird is.

key_points.html: Referee courses are usually run by the national federation.
At FITASC events each referee holds a valid federation certificate or card.
In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, a person without a certificate can only be an assistant referee, and only if the jury agrees.
The chief referee of an international event needs a FITASC qualification.
Start by helping an experienced referee at club shoots.

did_you_know.html: In both disciplines a referee at an international event must carry the current rules in the FITASC official languages.
